results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle of shipping requests from order retrieval through packaging and document generation, ensuring accurate consignee details, hazardous material compliance, and print-ready dispatch labels. Enables bundling of orders, validation of packaging instructions, and seamless handoff to warehouse execution.

features.title: Order Bundling Operations: Search, Bundle, Update, Export, and Print
features.description: Allows logistics operators to search for order lines by date, consignee, and other filters; move selected lines into a bundle with duplicate and consignee validation; remove lines via button or drag-and-drop; commit the bundle with voucher sequence allocation; navigate to order detail, packing instruction, and wording master screens; export a packed sheet to Excel; print a FAX shipment slip; and export grid data to Excel/CSV via ancestor pattern.

functions.label: Search for order lines using filters (Search)
functions.description: The user applies search filters to retrieve order lines that match specified criteria, loading them into the primary data grid for further processing. This enables logistics operators to locate relevant order lines efficiently.

functions.label: Add checked order lines to a bundle (Move to Bundle)
functions.description: The user selects one or more order lines from the search results and moves them into the bundle list, where the system validates the consignee and prevents duplicate entries. This groups lines for combined shipping or consignment.

functions.label: Remove selected lines from the bundle (Remove from Bundle)
functions.description: The user selects rows in the bundle list and deletes them, removing those order lines from the consignment group. This allows correcting grouping errors before finalizing the bundle.

functions.label: Drag and drop to remove a line from bundle (Drag-and-Drop Removal)
functions.description: The user can drag a row from the bundle list and drop it to remove that order line from the group. Two activation points exist: window-level and data grid-level, offering flexibility in inbox management.

functions.label: Finalize bundle and assign voucher sequence (Update/Commit)
functions.description: The user triggers final validation of the grouped order lines, and the system allocates a unique voucher sequence number, updating the relevant database tables. This officially creates the consignment group and prepares it for shipment.

functions.label: Export packing sheet to Excel (Export Packing Sheet to Excel)
functions.description: The user initiates an export that retrieves packing-related data from four supporting sources and automatically builds an Excel workbook with the packing sheet layout. The resulting file is saved locally for further use, such as sharing with warehouse staff.

functions.label: Print shipment slip in FAX layout (Print FAX Shipment Slip)
functions.description: The user prints a shipment slip formatted for FAX transmission with three rows per page, pulling the necessary data from shipment records. Although FAX sending capability is disabled in the current code, the printout retains the FAX-friendly layout for manual faxing.

functions.label: Export grid data to Excel or CSV (Ancestor Excel Export (Overridden))
functions.description: The user can export the current grid contents to an Excel or CSV file using a standard export pattern inherited from the ancestor window, which has been completely customised for this screen. This provides a quick way to extract raw data for external analysis.

functions.label: Open order details for the selected line (Navigate to Order Detail)
functions.description: The user selects an order line and navigates to the dedicated order detail window, passing the relevant keys. Upon returning, the system automatically refreshes the search results to reflect any changes made.

functions.label: Open packing instruction entry with consignee context (Navigate to Packing Instruction)
functions.description: The user navigates to the packing instruction window, carrying over consignee and date details from the current context. Access is restricted based on user role, and the search list is refreshed when the user returns.

functions.label: Open wording master reference data (Navigate to Wording Master)
functions.description: The user opens the wording master maintenance window for reference or editing of textual templates. No automatic refresh occurs when the window closes, so the user must manually re-trigger search if needed.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder MDI child window (w_pdqs_iraitabane) where logistics operators search for order lines, bundle them into consignment groups, update voucher allocations, navigate to related master data (order detail, packing instruction, wording master), export packing sheets to Excel, and print FAX shipment slips.
business_context.target_state: A React order bundling workspace (<OrderBundlingPanel />) backed by REST endpoints GET /api/v1/orders (search), POST /api/v1/bundles (move to bundle), DELETE /api/v1/bundles/{id} (remove), PUT /api/v1/bundles/{id}/commit (update voucher allocation), with side panels for related master data and server-side Excel/PDF generation for export and print.

user_stories.title: Commit Bundle with Voucher Sequence
user_stories.i_want_to: finalise the bundle by providing packing‑container information, approve the update, and have the system allocate a unique voucher sequence number and persist the bundle to all selected order lines
user_stories.so_that: the bundled consignment is formally registered and can be tracked under a single voucher

acceptance_criteria.given: the bundle contains at least one order line, the packing‑container widget has been filled with valid container details, and the user has clicked the Update button
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the update dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: a new voucher sequence number (format YYYYnnnnnn) is assigned, the sequence counter is persisted, all bundled order lines are stamped with the voucher and packing info, a success message '登録しました。' appears, and the bundle grid and packing widget are cleared

acceptance_criteria.given: the bundle is empty (no rows in dw_2)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: the operation is silently aborted and no database changes occur

acceptance_criteria.given: the packing‑container information has not been fully entered
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: a message '梱包容器情報が未入力です。' is shown and the commit is blocked

acceptance_criteria.given: the user sees the confirmation dialog
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks Cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the update is aborted and no changes are made to the database

acceptance_criteria.given: the database update for the sequence table or any bundled row fails
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the update
acceptance_criteria.then: the entire transaction is rolled back and a message '更新に失敗しました。' is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: the current fiscal year does not yet have a sequence counter row in M_DEVHASO_SEQ
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the update
acceptance_criteria.then: a new counter row is created starting at 1 for that year, and the remaining steps continue as normal

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: cb_update::clicked overrides ancestor. Performs a multi‑statement manual transaction against M_DEVHASO_SEQ (sequence table) and M_DEVHASO_PDQS (order line updates). All DML is embedded SQL under FATRA with explicit f_commit/f_rollback. Packing container validation is done via uo_konp.of_inpchk().
user_stories.migration_hint: React <BundleCommitPanel /> calls PUT /api/v1/bundles/{bundleId}/commit with packing‑container DTO. Server executes sequence‑table upsert then batch UPDATE to order lines inside a single @Transactional boundary. Rollback on any failure.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: The sequence‑counter allocation and all order‑line updates must execute within a single atomic database transaction. Partial success must never be committed.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle of shipping requests from order retrieval through packaging and document generation, ensuring accurate consignee details, hazardous material compliance, and print-ready dispatch labels. Enables bundling of orders, validation of packaging instructions, and seamless handoff to warehouse execution.

features.title: Dispatch Slip Print and Export for Order Requests
features.description: Enables users to search order requests with filter criteria, view results in a grid, select rows, and print dispatch slips via multi-page print buffer, with Excel export capability and status flag updates.

functions.label: Set up order request search with default filters (Screen Initialisation)
functions.description: When the dispatch slip print window opens, the system automatically binds database transaction objects and resets all filter fields to their default values. This gives the user a ready‑to‑use search form without any manual setup.

functions.label: Search order requests using filter criteria (Search)
functions.description: The user enters filter values and triggers a search, which dynamically builds a SQL WHERE clause and retrieves matching order requests into the grid. The system also computes bundling flags and enables the Excel export button upon successful retrieval.

functions.label: Reset search filters and results grid (Clear)
functions.description: This button is intended to reset the form by clearing all filter fields and the results grid. However, in its current implementation it executes unrelated debug code and is non‑functional, so the reset capability is unavailable to users.

functions.label: Select a row or sort grid by column (Grid Row Select/Column Sort)
functions.description: Clicking a row in the results grid selects that row for subsequent actions like printing. Clicking the header of a text‑based column sorts the grid ascending by that column, providing instant in‑memory feedback without a database round‑trip.

functions.label: Select all visible order requests for printing (Select All)
functions.description: When invoked, this hidden functionality sets the print flag on every visible row, marking them all as selected for dispatch slip printing. The button that would trigger this bulk selection is not exposed in the UI, so the feature is unreachable.

functions.label: Deselect all visible order requests from printing (Deselect All)
functions.description: This hidden feature clears the print flag on all visible rows, effectively deselecting any previously selected order requests for printing. The button remains hidden and inaccessible via the user interface, preventing use of this capability.

functions.label: Export search results to an Excel workbook (Excel Export)
functions.description: The user can export the full set of order request data displayed in the grid to an Excel file. After choosing a save location, the system retrieves all data, opens Excel through OLE automation, populates a 31‑column worksheet, and saves the workbook. This requires Microsoft Excel to be installed on the client machine.

functions.label: Print dispatch slips for selected order requests (Print Dispatch Slip)
functions.description: After a user confirmation, the system opens the operating system’s print dialog. For each checked order request row, it retrieves detailed data, assembles a multi‑page print layout, sends it to the printer, and then marks the request as printed (PRTENDFLG='1') in the database. The grid refreshes to reflect the updated print status.

functions.label: Close the dispatch slip print window (Close)
functions.description: The user ends the dispatch slip printing session by closing the window. This action terminates the window and any associated operations, returning focus to the parent application.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder window (w_pdqs_iraiden_print) where users search for order requests using filter fields, view results in a DataWindow grid, select rows, and print dispatch slips. Includes Excel export via OLE automation and updates a print status flag after printing.
business_context.target_state: A React order request print management page (<OrderRequestPrint />) backed by REST endpoints for search (GET /api/v1/order-requests), print (POST /api/v1/order-requests/print), and export (GET /api/v1/order-requests/export), with server-side print dispatch and status tracking.

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: PowerBuilder window w_pdqs_iraiden_print, dw_data::sqlpreview dynamically rewrites WHERE clause using string concatenation from sle_loginid, em_from, em_to fields. cb_retrieve::clicked triggers u_retrieve. SQL injection risk. Grid sort via dw_data::u_sort (in-memory SetSort/Sort).
user_stories.migration_hint: Implement as GET /api/v1/order-requests with parameterized query parameters (staffCode, dateFrom, dateTo, printStatus). Use React <OrderRequestSearch /> component with server-side pagination. Sorting via query string orderBy/orderDir.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All database queries must use parameterised statements to prevent SQL injection, replacing the legacy dynamic SQL string concatenation.

user_stories.title: Print Dispatch Slips
user_stories.i_want_to: print the dispatch slip documents for the selected order requests and mark them as printed
user_stories.so_that: the warehouse can fulfil the shipment and the records are removed from the outstanding print queue

acceptance_criteria.given: at least one row is selected for printing and the user confirms the operation
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Print button and proceeds through the print dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: the system prints the dispatch slips for all selected records, updates their print status flag to 'Printed' in the database, commits the transaction, refreshes the grid, and displays '印刷が完了しました。'

acceptance_criteria.given: a database error occurs while updating the print flag after a slip has been printed
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Print button and the update fails
acceptance_criteria.then: the entire batch transaction is rolled back, the print flag remains unchanged, and the error message '更新に失敗しました。TABLE:M_DEVHASO_PDQS' is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: the user is about to print
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Print button and then cancels the confirmation dialog or the system print dialog
acceptance_criteria.then: no printing occurs and no database changes are made

acceptance_criteria.given: no rows are selected for printing
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Print button
acceptance_criteria.then: no printing occurs and no message is displayed; the system silently does nothing

acceptance_criteria.given: the logged‑in user belongs to a department other than 'VOR'
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Print button
acceptance_criteria.then: a warning confirmation message is shown ('セイグンさんが実施する処理ですが、よろしいですか？') before allowing the user to proceed

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: cb_print::clicked overrides ancestor, loops selected rows (printflg='1'), retrieves detail via dw_printdata, builds multi‑page print buffer, calls PrintSetup() / f_print(), then executes manual UPDATE M_DEVHASO_PDQS SET PRTENDFLG='1' keyed on ADYYSEQ or composite key. Single f_commit(FATRA) after loop or f_rollback on first UPDATE failure. Department‑dependent confirmation via M_TANTOKAN lookup.
user_stories.migration_hint: Server‑side PDF generation (e.g., Jasper Reports) triggered by POST /api/v1/order-requests/print with selected keys. Per‑record optimistic locking on PRTENDFLG before UPDATE. Single transactional batch commit/rollback. Department‑based confirmation wording resolved from JWT claims.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All print slip generation and status flag updates must execute within an atomic database transaction with full rollback on any step failure.
Every print status change (PRTENDFLG) must be logged with user identity, timestamp, and before/after values.

user_stories.title: Screen Initialisation with Default Filters
user_stories.i_want_to: see the dispatch slip screen open with default filter settings (Not Yet Printed selected, dates blank, grid empty)
user_stories.so_that: I can immediately begin working with the standard unprinted shipment list

acceptance_criteria.given: the dispatch slip print window is being opened

features.title: Document Text Master Record Maintenance (CRUD, Export)
features.description: Enables authorised users to view, insert, delete, and update wording master records (devmongon) in the SIL00.M_DEVMONGON table, and export the full grid content to Excel. Includes role‑based read‑only enforcement on window open.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint – w_pdqs_devmongon (Document Text Maintenance), S.5 Events #1–#7

functions.label: Load wording master data and apply role-based permissions (Screen Initialization)
functions.description: On opening the window, the system retrieves all wording master records from the database and displays them in a grid. If the user’s role lacks edit permissions, the grid is set to read-only mode, preventing modifications. This ensures data visibility while enforcing access control.

functions.label: Stage deletion of a wording master record (Row Delete)
functions.description: User can select a row and initiate deletion, which removes it from the on-screen grid buffer without affecting the database immediately. The deletion is staged until the user clicks Update, allowing them to review changes before committing. This provides a safe, reversible editing experience.

functions.label: Stage a new wording master record for entry (Row Insert)
functions.description: When the user wants to add a new wording master record, inserting a blank row into the grid allows data entry. The row is held in the local buffer and can be edited, deleted, or copied until the user commits changes with the Update function. This staged insertion encourages accurate data capture before persisting.

functions.label: Commit all pending wording master changes to database (Update)
functions.description: After reviewing staged additions, deletions, and modifications, the user triggers Update. The system first checks for unsaved changes, validates data integrity, and asks for confirmation before writing all pending changes to the wording master table. Once committed, the grid refreshes to reflect the current database state, ensuring consistency.

functions.label: Export wording master data to Excel or CSV (Excel Export)
functions.description: Users can export the currently displayed wording master records to an external file for reporting or offline analysis. The function checks that the grid is not empty before proceeding, and reports success or failure to the user. This enables easy data sharing and archival outside the application.

functions.label: Close the wording master maintenance window (Close)
functions.description: Clicking Close shuts the current child window and returns the user to the parent screen or sheet from which the wording master maintenance was opened. This is a standard navigation action with no additional processing, providing a straightforward exit from the management view.

functions.label: Trigger focused button action with Enter key (Enter Key Press)
functions.description: For keyboard-driven efficiency, pressing the Enter key activates the currently focused button on the form, such as save, delete, or export. This allows power users to operate the window without a mouse, speeding up data management tasks.

business_context.target_state: A React document text master management page (<DocumentTextMaster />) backed by REST API endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE /api/v1/document-texts) with role‑based access control and Excel export capability.

user_stories.title: Save Document Text Master Changes
user_stories.i_want_to: insert new wording records, delete existing ones, and modify record texts in the grid, then commit all pending changes with a single Update action
user_stories.so_that: I can efficiently maintain the standard wording library with accurate current text content and unique codes

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has edit permission, has made valid changes (inserted new rows with unique codes and non‑blank text, deleted rows, or modified text), and the data passes all validation
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update (更新) button and confirms the operation
acceptance_criteria.then: all changes are saved to the database, a success message “登録しました。” is shown, and the grid refreshes with the latest data

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has left the document code or text blank on a row
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: a validation error message is displayed (e.g., “文言ｺｰﾄﾞが入力されていません。” or “文言内容が入力されていません。”), the save is not performed, and the offending field is focused

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has entered a document code that already exists in another row in the same batch
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: a duplicate key error message “同じデータが存在しているため、更新する事が出来ません。” is displayed, the offending row is highlighted, and the save is aborted

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has not made any modifications since the last retrieve
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: an informational message “登録（変更）データがありません。” is displayed and no save is attempted

acceptance_criteria.given: the Update button has focus and the user has pending changes
acceptance_criteria.when: the user presses the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.then: the Update action is triggered as if the button were clicked

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has changes and clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.when: the confirmation dialog appears and the user clicks Cancel
acceptance_criteria.then: the save is aborted and the data remains in the grid for further editing

acceptance_criteria.given: a user with a view‑only role attempts to trigger the Update action (e.g., by a direct API call)
acceptance_criteria.when: the save request is sent
acceptance_criteria.then: the server returns a 403 Forbidden and no data is saved

acceptance_criteria.given: the user has retrieved data, but another user has modified the same record before this user’s update
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clicks the Update button
acceptance_criteria.then: an optimistic lock conflict is detected, a 409 Conflict error is returned, and a message about stale data is displayed

user_stories.technical_notes: The Update flow: cb_update (ancestor) calls fw_ck_dwchange(2) to check changes, then u_nullchek (generic required field), then u_updtchek (concrete: blank check + fw_find_key duplicate check), then confirmation dialog, then u_update: This.Update() on dw_data (dw_pdqs_devmongon) with f_commit(FATRA) on success. Row insert (cb_rowins) and row delete (cb_rowdel) operate on the buffer. Enter key in ancestor key event triggers focused button click.
user_stories.migration_hint: PUT /api/v1/document-texts with batch save endpoint accepting array of rows with rowAction, origin (for optimistic lock), and value. Server-side validation (non‑blank, unique code across batch), duplicate check, and RBAC enforcement (role check) must be implemented.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All update operations must execute within an atomic database transaction with full rollback on any step failure.
Server-side role-based access control must reject write attempts from users with viewer role with HTTP 403.

results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle of shipping requests from order retrieval through packaging and document generation, ensuring accurate consignee details, hazardous material compliance, and print-ready dispatch labels. Enables bundling of orders, validation of packaging instructions, and seamless handoff to warehouse execution.

features.title: Consignment Shipment Search, Update, Export, and Print
features.description: Enables users to search and retrieve consignment shipment data, manage comments and label rows, edit comment codes with master validation, and commit changes across four grid sections. Supports Excel export and paginated printing of shipment sub-reports.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint w_pdqs_konsas, S.5 Events #1-#14 (consignment shipment processing screen)

functions.label: Load consignment shipment search window with header and grid data (Window Open)
functions.description: When the user opens the Consignment Shipment Search window, the system loads consignee header information and populates the initial grid content, allowing the user to start a search or view existing data.

functions.label: Retrieve consignment data into all grids based on search criteria (Retrieve Data)
functions.description: Based on user input and the selected mode (Input or Confirm), the system executes a server-side search and loads results into the main data grid and three additional grids. This provides a complete view of consignment shipment information and comments.

functions.label: Move a comment row upward in the list (Move Row Up)
functions.description: Users can reorder comment rows by moving a selected row up one position. The swap occurs instantly on the client without a database call, helping organize comments in the desired sequence.

functions.label: Move a comment row downward in the list (Move Row Down)
functions.description: Users can shift a selected comment row down one position to reorder the list. The in-memory operation provides immediate feedback without server interaction.

functions.label: Select all label rows for bulk actions (Select All Labels)
functions.description: The user can mark every row in the label grid as selected with a single action. This client-side batch update enables quick preparation for subsequent operations like delete or export.

functions.label: Clear all label row selections (Deselect All Labels)
functions.description: Users can deselect all currently selected label rows at once. This resets the grid to an unselected state, allowing a fresh selection.

functions.label: Validate comment code against master data on entry (Comment Item Changed)
functions.description: When a user modifies a comment code in the grid, the system checks it against the master comment table in real time. This prevents invalid codes from being saved, ensuring data integrity.

functions.label: Add a new blank comment row (Row Insert)
functions.description: Users can insert an empty row into the comments grid to enter a new comment. The row is added on the client side instantly and can be filled in before saving.

functions.label: Remove the selected comment row (Row Delete)
functions.description: The user can delete the currently highlighted comment row from the grid. The deletion is local until the update is committed.

functions.label: Save all grid changes to the database (Update/Save)
functions.description: After making edits, the user can save changes across all four data grids. The system performs validation, confirmation, and then persists the updates to the database, refreshing the display with the latest data.

functions.label: Export consignment data to an Excel workbook (Excel Export)
functions.description: Users can generate a complete Excel workbook containing the consignment shipment and comment data. The export relies on client-side OLE Automation, which will be modernized to server-side generation for future releases.

functions.label: Print consignment data with paginated sub-reports (Print)
functions.description: The user can print the consignment details, with the system automatically splitting data into pages of 56 rows each and composing sub-reports. This ensures formatted output suitable for physical documentation.

functions.label: Choose a comment code from a popup list (Comment Code Popup)
functions.description: When entering a comment, users can open a modal selection window to search and pick a valid comment code from the master list. The chosen code is returned and inserted into the grid cell.

functions.label: Close the consignment shipment search window (Close)
functions.description: The user can close the modal window to return to the previous screen. This action discards any unsaved changes and completes the session.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder modal window (w_pdqs_konsas) where users input consignment shipment criteria, retrieve data into four grids (dw_data, dw_1, dw_2, dw_3), manage comment rows and labels, validate comment codes against a master table, and commit updates. Export and print operations use client-side OLE Automation and Pagination logic.
business_context.target_state: A React consignment shipment management page (<ConsignmentShipmentManager />) backed by REST endpoints such as GET /api/v1/consignment-shipments?mode=… and PUT /api/v1/consignment-shipments/{id}/comments, with server-side Excel generation and PDF-based printing.

user_stories.technical_notes: dw_data (dw_pdqs_devhaso_memo) provides the comment grid. Row insert (cb_rowins) calls ancestor f_insert, row delete (cb_rowdel) calls f_delete. Comment code validation via dw_data::itemchanged (EVENT-007) and doubleclicked (EVENT-008) performs SELECT on M_DEVMONGON. Reorder via cb_up/cb_dwn (EVENT-003/004) swaps fields in-memory. Save (cb_update) triggers u_update which deletes all M_DEVHASO_MEMO rows for the key and re-inserts non-blank rows with new SEQ.
user_stories.migration_hint: PUT /api/v1/consignment-shipments/{niukcd}/{nktannm}/{niwatadt}/comments with an array of comment objects, supporting reordering via sequenceNumber. Implement real-time code validation via GET /api/v1/comment-master/{mongoncd}. Use React grid component with inline editing, drag-and-drop reordering, and a popup selector for code picker.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All comment saves must execute within an atomic database transaction that also covers other grid edits (product info, labels, inspection) to preserve the legacy multi-table commit behavior.

features.title: Container Dimension Entry and Consolidation Selection Validation
features.description: Enables operators to select a container via a double‑click picker popup, view auto‑populated container name and standard dimensions, manually adjust length, width, height, and quantity, and execute validation before saving to ensure data integrity in packaging consolidation workflows.
features.source: SRS UIBlueprint uo_pdqs_konpoyoki (custom visual user object) – S.5 Events #1‑#8

functions.label: Look up container name and dimensions from code (Container Code Changed)
functions.description: When the user enters or changes the container code, the system performs a live SQL lookup using the FATRA transaction to retrieve the container name and standard dimensions (length, width, height). If no matching container is found, the fields are silently cleared to indicate an invalid code.

functions.label: Capture modified container name for saving (Container Name Changed)
functions.description: The operator may manually edit the container name after it is populated. This change is stored in the application state for inclusion in the save operation, without making a server call.

functions.label: Capture adjusted length dimension for saving (Length Changed)
functions.description: The operator can modify the length of the container entry. The updated value is synchronized into a variable for later persistence, with no immediate server interaction.

functions.label: Capture adjusted width dimension for saving (Width Changed)
functions.description: The operator can modify the width of the container entry. The updated value is held in application state to be saved as part of the container data.

functions.label: Capture adjusted height dimension for saving (Height Changed)
functions.description: The operator can modify the height of the container entry. The change is stored locally and will be committed when the save operation is executed.

functions.label: Capture adjusted container quantity for saving (Quantity Changed)
functions.description: The operator can adjust the number of containers. This modified quantity is retained in the session state for inclusion in the final save.

functions.label: Validate container entry data before saving (Validation Execution)
functions.description: Prior to saving the container dimensions and quantity, the host window triggers an input validation check to confirm that all required fields are correctly filled. This validation gate may prevent the save if data does not meet business rules, protecting data quality.

functions.label: Open container selection dialog from code field (Container Code Double-Click)
functions.description: By double-clicking the container code field, the operator opens a modal selection window that displays available containers. Choosing a container populates the code, name, and standard dimensions back into the form, streamlining data entry.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder custom visual user object (uo_pdqs_konpoyoki) where logistics operators enter container dimensions and quantity. Container lookup is performed via a modal popup (w_pub_pop_konsas) triggered by a double‑click on the container code; a live SQL lookup retrieves the container name and standard dimensions using the FATRA transaction. Manual adjustments to length, width, height, and quantity are synced to instance variables, and a validation gate (of_inpchk) is invoked by the hosting window before saving.
business_context.target_state: A React container line‑item entry component (<ContainerEntryWidget />) backed by REST microservices (GET /api/v1/containers/{code} for standard dimensions, PUT /api/v1/packaging/items/{id} for updates). Inline validation, modal picker integration, and optimistic real‑time sync replace the legacy PowerBuilder instance‑variable pattern.

The S.3 controls table is unavailable; therefore bounding_box.controls[] and s3_row_refs[] are left empty. The widget is user‑facing (container code, name, dimensions, quantity). A post‑generation enrichment step should populate controls from the S.3 table once available.

S.5 Event #4: Length Changed – syncs length into instance variable
S.5 Event #5: Width Changed – syncs width into instance variable
S.5 Event #6: Height Changed – syncs height into instance variable
S.5 Event #7: Quantity Changed – syncs quantity into instance variable

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy trigger: sle_konpyoucd.modified event in uo_pdqs_konpoyoki. Executes two embedded SQL SELECT statements against the FATRA transaction object (not SQLCA). The second query joins M_KONSAS with an aggregated subquery on M_M3KETEI to fetch MAX(TATE), MAX(YOKO), MAX(TAKASA). The original 'not found' MessageBox is commented out (legacy defect), resulting in silent clearing. Trace IDs: TRCE-UI-uo_pdqs_konpoyoki‑L515‑519, L526‑538.

user_stories.technical_notes: Legacy: instance variables id_konptate, id_konpyoko, id_konptakasa, il_konpkosu are updated on every keystroke via modified events (em_length.modified etc.). Validation gate of_inpchk() is called externally by the host window before save; it returns 0 to block save on various failures (negative values, all‑or‑nothing size rule when no code, mandatory quantity when pi_chkflg=1). All dimension inputs use EditMask format ##0.0000 with 4‑decimal precision. Trace IDs: TRCE-UI-uo_pdqs_konpoyoki‑L83‑156.
user_stories.migration_hint: React component <ContainerDimensionsEditor /> with controlled numeric inputs (format ##0.0000). Expose a validate(chkFlag) method that returns field‑level errors or passes. On parent save, call validate() and display inline errors. Use Decimal or BigDecimal to preserve 4‑decimal precision.

results.module_business_name: Vendor Code Lookup and Selection (Reusable Component)
results.module_business_description: Governs the lifecycle of shipping requests from order retrieval through packaging and document generation, ensuring accurate consignee details, hazardous material compliance, and print-ready dispatch labels. Enables bundling of orders, validation of packaging instructions, and seamless handoff to warehouse execution.

features.title: External Vendor Code Lookup and Selection
features.description: Enables users to search and select an external vendor code (gaisocd) via a popup window. Supports double-click lookup, manual code validation against the master table, list browsing with keyboard and button selection, and cancellation handling.

functions.label: Validate vendor code existence against master data (Code Existence Validation)
functions.description: When a user types or selects an external vendor code, the system verifies that code against the M_GAISO master table. This ensures only valid codes are accepted before proceeding.

functions.label: Open vendor code lookup popup with initial selection (Popup Window Open)
functions.description: A user action opens a modal popup that loads the full list of available vendor codes. The first row is automatically selected, or a 'No data' message is displayed if the list is empty.

functions.label: Forward user keystrokes to the active control (Window-Level Key Press)
functions.description: When a user presses a key while the popup is open, the raw key event is re-dispatched to the relevant control, such as the list or input field. This ensures keyboard shortcuts and navigation keys work correctly within the window.

functions.label: Open vendor code lookup on double-click and apply result (Double-Click Code Field)
functions.description: When the user double-clicks the external vendor code field, a modal popup appears to browse and select a code. After closing the popup, the chosen code is placed in the field and validated for existence.

functions.label: Select highlighted vendor code with Enter key (Enter Key on List)

functions.label: Cancel vendor code lookup and clear selection (Close Button Click)

features.title: Packing Group Code Lookup and Selection
features.description: Enables users to enter a packing group code, validate its existence against the database, and browse the full packing group master list through a modal picker supporting selection and cancellation.

functions.label: Validate packing group code entry (u_post_itemchange)
functions.description: When a user enters a packing group code and the field loses focus, the system trims and null-checks the input, then performs a server-side validation lookup against the database. This ensures only existing and valid packing group codes are accepted, reducing data entry errors.

functions.label: Display packing group master list in picker (w_pub_pop_kongrp.open)
functions.description: Opening the packing group picker invokes a server call to retrieve the full master list of codes, which are then displayed for user selection. If no records exist, a 'No data' message clearly informs the user, preventing confusion.

functions.label: Open packing group picker on double-click (OpenWithParm)
functions.description: Double-clicking the packing group code field launches the modal picker window, which loads the master code list. This provides a fast, browse-based alternative to manual code entry for users.

functions.label: Confirm selected packing group code (SelectButton_Click)
functions.description: Clicking the 'Select' button after highlighting a row in the picker returns the chosen packing group code to the main form. If no row is selected, an empty value is returned, leaving the previous input unchanged.

functions.label: Cancel packing group selection (CloseButton_Click)
functions.description: The 'Close' button aborts the selection process and returns no value, keeping the original code field unchanged. This lets users exit the picker without altering any data.

functions.label: Quick-select packing group by double-click (gridRow_dblclick)
functions.description: Double-clicking any row in the picker list immediately selects that packing group code and closes the window, mirroring the 'Select' button action. This streamlines the selection workflow for fast data entry.

functions.label: Select packing group with Enter key (dwnkey_enter)
functions.description: Pressing the Enter key while a row is highlighted in the picker triggers the same selection logic as a double-click, confirming the choice instantly. This provides keyboard accessibility for efficient, mouse-free operation.

business_context.current_state: A PowerBuilder custom visual user object (uo_pub_kongrpcd) providing packing group code input and validation, with a modal popup (w_pub_pop_kongrp) for browsing and selecting from the master list. The popup offers select, close, double-click, and keyboard navigation.
business_context.target_state: A React component (<PackingGroupSelector />) backed by GET /api/v1/packing-groups for master list retrieval and POST /api/v1/packing-groups/validate for code lookup, with a modal picker for interactive selection and cancellation.

user_stories.title: Confirm Orphan Status of PDQS Dead-Code Artifacts
user_stories.i_want_to: review the five orphan DataWindow artifacts (dw_pdqs_devhaso_excel2, dw_pdqs_haraidashi_print_bk, dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den, dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den1, dw_pdqs_iraiden_print_den_bk) to determine whether they are still called by any active window or menu
user_stories.so_that: I can correctly classify them as dead code that can be retired without migration effort or as live artifacts that require modernisation, avoiding unnecessary development work

acceptance_criteria.given: the migration QA engineer has access to the five PDQS dead‑code candidate artifacts and the application call‑graph report
acceptance_criteria.when: they run a dependency analysis across all .srw/.sru window and menu objects
acceptance_criteria.then: the analysis confirms that no PowerScript caller references any of the five DataWindow objects and the status is recorded as 'confirmed orphan'

acceptance_criteria.given: the call‑graph analysis has completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the report shows that at least one of the five DataWindows is referenced by an active window object
acceptance_criteria.then: the artifact is removed from the dead‑code list and a migration planning task is created for that artifact

acceptance_criteria.given: the migration QA engineer attempts to analyse the call graph but some .srw files are unavailable or incomplete
acceptance_criteria.when: they review the partial results
acceptance_criteria.then: the artifacts with missing evidence are flagged for manual code‑base review and a follow‑up meeting is scheduled with the original developer if available

user_stories.technical_notes: The MFU contains five isolated DataWindow objects with no visible callers in the provided payload: dw_pdqs_devhaso_excel2 (Excel export, ADYYSEQ), dw_pdqs_haraidashi_print_bk (payout slip, JYUCYUNO+HINMEINO+BUNNO), dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den, dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den1 (FAX shipping slips, dual key), dw_pdqs_iraiden_print_den_bk (multi‑copy print booklet). All objects are marked updatewhereclause=yes but no Update() or Transaction Object binding was found, confirming read‑only report/print intent. Investigation must verify call‑graph completeness before decommissioning.
user_stories.migration_hint: Run a full‑codebase grep for each DataWindow name (dw_pdqs_devhaso_excel2, dw_pdqs_haraidashi_print_bk, dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den, dw_pdqs_iraiden_fax_den1, dw_pdqs_iraiden_print_den_bk) across all .srw / .sru files. If no window/script references are found, retire the artifacts. If a caller is discovered, create a separate migration task to implement the corresponding print/export API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/mod-pdqs/devhaso-excel, /api/v1/pdqs/haraidashi-voucher).
